subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which three logic gates are included in the OCR J277 specification?
questions.explain: J277 requires only the AND, OR and NOT gates.

questions.q: By what other name is the NOT gate commonly known?
questions.explain: The NOT gate inverts its input, so it is also called an inverter.

questions.q: An AND gate outputs 1 only when:
questions.explain: An AND gate gives an output of 1 only if every input is 1.

questions.q: An OR gate outputs 1 when:
questions.explain: An OR gate outputs 1 if one or more of its inputs is 1.

questions.q: How many inputs does a NOT gate have?
questions.explain: A NOT gate has a single input and a single output.

questions.q: A truth table for a circuit with two inputs has how many rows?
questions.explain: With 2 inputs there are 2 to the power 2 = 4 possible input combinations.

questions.q: A truth table for a circuit with three inputs has how many rows?
questions.explain: With 3 inputs there are 2 to the power 3 = 8 possible input combinations.

questions.q: What does a truth table list in its columns for a logic circuit?
options: The inputs and the resulting output
The binary value of denary numbers
questions.explain: A truth table records every input combination and the output produced.

questions.q: An AND gate has inputs A = 1 and B = 0. What is its output?
questions.explain: An AND gate outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1, so here the output is 0.

questions.q: An OR gate has inputs A = 0 and B = 0. What is its output?
questions.explain: An OR gate outputs 0 only when all inputs are 0.

questions.q: A NOT gate is given an input of 1. What is its output?
questions.explain: A NOT gate inverts its input, so 1 becomes 0.

questions.q: A two-input gate outputs 1 for every input combination except when both inputs are 0. Which gate is it?
questions.explain: This is the OR gate, which outputs 0 only when both inputs are 0.

questions.q: A two-input gate outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1 and 0 otherwise. Which gate is it?
questions.explain: Only the AND gate outputs 1 exclusively when both inputs are 1.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of drawing a truth table?
options: To show the output for every possible combination of inputs
To convert denary numbers into binary
To measure the voltage in a circuit
To list the price of each logic gate
questions.explain: A truth table sets out the output for all possible input combinations of a circuit.

questions.q: A NOT gate is connected to the output of an AND gate. For which input combination does this circuit output 0?
questions.explain: The AND gives 1 only when both inputs are 1, and the NOT then inverts that 1 to 0.

questions.q: When two logic gates are combined, the output of the first gate becomes:
options: an input to the second gate
the final answer, ignoring the second gate
the same as a truth table row count
questions.explain: In a combined circuit, one gate's output feeds in as an input to the next gate.

questions.q: A circuit gives output = NOT (A AND B). With A = 1 and B = 1, the output is:
questions.explain: A AND B = 1, and NOT 1 = 0.

questions.q: A circuit gives output = A OR (NOT B). With A = 0 and B = 1, the output is:
questions.explain: NOT B = 0, and 0 OR 0 = 0.

questions.q: A circuit gives output = (A AND B) OR C. With A = 1, B = 0 and C = 1, the output is:
questions.explain: A AND B = 0, and 0 OR 1 = 1.

questions.q: A circuit gives output = A AND B AND C. With A = 1, B = 1 and C = 0, the output is:
questions.explain: An AND is 1 only when all inputs are 1, and here C = 0, so the output is 0.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Computer Science (J277) specification; Boolean Logic
